findings.reason: as written the node implements a claim one number above the attempt it guards, so the dispatch door stays unguarded while the resume-path cases pass, and the section must state which record the claim is derived from (the pointer as it stood before the launch) or the claim is decorative.
findings.text: the deliverable says every launch of an existing run id reserves its attempt through `claim_next_attempt`, but that function derives its number as `int(record.get("attempt") or 1) + 1` (resumption.py:398) and expects a record naming the attempt already taken, as the resume path passes it; on the dispatch path the record already carries the attempt being launched (dispatch.py:3013 writes `"attempt": attempt` into the pointer, and :3372 hands `int(record["attempt"])` to `_prepare_attempt_records`), so a claim taken there reserves attempt N+1 while attempt N is the one starting, and `_retired_attempt_ended`'s new in-flight reading — which looks for a claim on the attempt `attempt.json` names — finds no claim for that attempt at all

findings.reason: the section's stated exit clause does not hold on the path it adds the claim to, so the repair would strand every dispatch killed inside its own window, and done-when case 3 exercises only the pointer-short resume shape and cannot catch it.
findings.text: the section states "A claim held past `LAUNCH_WINDOW_SECONDS` with no worker record is abandoned, as `_claim_may_be_reclaimed` already decides, so a launcher killed inside the window leaves the run launchable", but `_claim_may_be_reclaimed` (resumption.py:366) answers `False` on `current == claimed` before it ever reads the claim's age (:378-382), and the dispatch path writes the pointer's attempt to the new number at dispatch.py:3316 before `_prepare_attempt_records` at :3369 — so a dispatch killed after the pointer write leaves `read_pointer().attempt == claimed`, the claim is never reclaimed at any age, and the in-flight reading refuses that attempt for good

findings.reason: the followup prompt is the text a dispatched node is given, and it names the wrong file plus the refactor the section deliberately dropped, which invites exactly the scope creep the section was rewritten to avoid.
findings.text: the open followup that invokes the section (`f-arolw-013`) states it "writes `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py` and `reckon/crew/resumption.py`", while the section now writes `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py` and the new test — so the one hand-off a builder reads points at `resumption.py`, the reader refactor an earlier review had removed from this section, and omits the dispatch path where the second door actually lives

findings.reason: the queue releases on declared waits, so this edge holds the plan's last section behind an unrelated one, and the real prerequisite (§12) is not declared at all.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` declares `"s13":["a-run-has-one-live-worker#s10"]`, a wait on s10, but s13's stated prerequisites are §11's refusal behaviour and §12's landed receipts (both done), and nothing in its deliverable consumes §10's pre-worktree live-holder check
